description: Cockpit section only. Damaged at Efogi, Papua New Guinea 05/09/2008 through fatigue; recovered to Townsville for investigation and the cockpit restored for display. Confirmed by the Department of Defence announcement of the centre's reopening, 20 August 2025. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Vietnam veteran that flew 3026 hours in-theatre with 9 Squadron and returned to Australia aboard HMAS Sydney in November 1971; later modified to Bushranger configuration. Confirmed by the Department of Defence announcement of the centre's reopening, 20 August 2025.

Delivered 09/1955. Formerly the gate guard at RAAF Wagga Wagga. Confirmed by the Department of Defence announcement of the centre's reopening, 20 August 2025. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Forward air control PC-9; flew on Exercise Pitch Black at RAAF Tindal 09/08/2018 and was flown to Townsville and transferred to the heritage centre in 09/2019. Confirmed by the Department of Defence announcement of the centre's reopening, 20 August 2025. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Delivered 04/08/1967 and withdrawn 04/1987. Restored at Amberley and now displayed at Townsville in 76 Squadron markings. Confirmed by the Department of Defence announcement of the centre's reopening, 20 August 2025. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Formerly the gate guard at RAAF Wagga Wagga and later at Bandiana Army Barracks. ADF-Serials records it as currently at the RAAF Heritage Centre, Townsville. It is not among the five aircraft named in the August 2025 reopening announcement, so it is treated here as not yet on public display.

Served with 1 AFTS Pearce and was Instructional Airframe No. 24 at RSTT Wagga Wagga; later a spares source for the airworthy restoration of A79-636. ADF-Serials records it as under restoration for static display at the Townsville heritage centre.
